name: Manual / commercial geosteering practice: typewell (type-log) correlation, TVT modelling, ROGII StarSteer, Landmark and H&P segment/heat-map correlation
authors_org: Industry practice; ROGII (StarSteer, AutoSteer, multi-typewell with variable thickness in 2025.2); Landmark Graphics (Lagenwalter, Poland, Daffin; patent US20130238306A1 / US10318662B2); Helmerich & Payne (M. Willerth; automated heat-map geosteering, IADC/SPE 2022; Bayesian-Viterbi method, SPE/IADC Drilling Conference 2023); SES 'Geosteering Mechanics' practitioner notes (makinhole.com)
year: Practice codified 2010-2025 (patent filed 2010, granted 2019; H&P 2022 and 2023; StarSteer 2025.2 multi-typewell webinar Oct 2025)
code_availability: None. StarSteer / AutoSteer and H&P tools are proprietary; the patent describes the workflow only.
evidence_level: Mixed: granted patent text (read via Google Patents), trade-press article (Drilling Contractor), practitioner web notes, vendor pages; the SPE 2023 Bayesian-Viterbi paper is known from abstract/search snippets only (full text paywalled, HTTP 403).
extreme_summary: Experts convert lateral GR to TVT by assuming a piecewise-planar formation (dip segments plus fault throws plus stretch/squeeze) and fitting it until lateral GR matches the typewell; repeated-layer ties are broken by continuity from an unambiguous landing, preference for few segments, peak/valley sequence-and-spacing matching, regional dip from offsets, and (hardware permitting) azimuthal up/down gamma.
task_definition: Estimate the bit's stratigraphic position (TVT relative to a typewell / target top) along the lateral in real time, i.e. a mapping MD -> TVT, from lateral GR and trajectory, in order to steer the well in zone.
inputs: Lateral LWD gamma ray (sometimes resistivity, azimuthal/imaging gamma, continuous inclination); survey trajectory (MD, inclination, azimuth, TVD/Z); one or several typewells / offset vertical pilots; regional 3D structure grids or seismic surfaces; the landing (build) section where the well crosses stratigraphy steeply and correlation is least ambiguous.
target_parameterisation: Explicit structural model: a sequence of segments, each with an apparent dip, optional fault throw at segment boundaries and optional thickness scaling. TVT at each MD follows from TVD minus the modelled surface depth, i.e. the structural-coordinate form (u = TVT + Z) with a dip state. The typewell is projected parallel to the modelled surfaces ('TVT type log'); the inflection point where wellbore inclination equals apparent dip marks a TVT extremum.
output_representation: Classic manual practice: a single best interpretation (polyline of dip segments + faults). Commercial automation adds multiple scenario interpretations per lateral (StarSteer: several interpretations from multiple offset wells), probability heat maps over stratigraphic depth vs MD (H&P 2022), and a Viterbi best path over a Bayesian state space with complexity-weighted likelihood (H&P 2023).
architecture: Human-in-the-loop fitting: (1) establish a 3D interpreted surface / regional dip; (2) initialise a straight-line 2D model; (3) compute predicted lateral GR from the typewell using the vertical distance the wellbore penetrates the modelled formation at each sample; (4) segment by segment, adjust dip and fault sliders until predicted and actual GR segments match (optional cross-correlation QC curve); (5) place tie lines/markers where the curves diverge and open a new segment; (6) push the 2D model back to 3D surface hardpoints. Automated variants replace step 4 with misfit heat maps plus path search (H&P), Viterbi on a Bayesian state space (H&P 2023), a particle filter plus DTW against one or more offsets (Geosciences 2024), or a proprietary ML AutoSteer trained on thousands of wells (ROGII).
core_mechanism: A strong structural prior: beds are locally planar, so TVT(MD) is piecewise-linear along hole with few breakpoints, and the lateral GR must reproduce the typewell GR under this geometric warp. Repeated-layer ambiguity is resolved by (a) continuity from an unambiguous start (landing/heel, 'one wrong pick and subsequent picks are often all wrong'), (b) a parsimony/complexity preference for fewer dip changes and faults, (c) matching the sequence and spacing of peaks and valleys rather than a single feature's amplitude, (d) stretch/squeeze diagnosis: features stretched along MD mean near-parallel drilling, compressed means crossing, which reveals dip relative to inclination, (e) regional dip from offsets and 3D grids as a prior, (f) azimuthal gamma high-side vs low-side to tell up-section from down-section exits, (g) multiple typewells / variable thickness for lateral facies and thickness change.
training_objective: Not learned. Manual: visual GR misfit minimisation with parsimony judgement. Automated: GR misfit (heat-map probability) plus geometric/complexity prior; Bayesian likelihood with a complexity-related correctness prior (H&P 2023).
decoding: Manual: a single most-plausible path chosen by the geosteerer. H&P 2023: Viterbi best path over the full stratigraphic state space. H&P 2022: path through the heat map plus human control points. All mode-seeking, path-level.
metric_consistent_decode: Mode-seeking (single interpretation / Viterbi). Not Bayes-optimal for pooled RMSE; practice optimises in-zone footage, where committing to one band is rational, whereas pooled RMSE favours the posterior mean.
evidence_scope: Whole lateral from landing to current bit, plus typewell(s), offset wells and regional structure (multi-well context).
prefix_conditioning: Central: interpretation is sequential and anchored at the already-interpreted section (landing curve and earlier lateral); dip is calibrated during landing (SES 'Block' parameters) and new segments extend the existing polyline.
propose_vs_select: Propose-then-select: several candidate interpretations (different typewells, fault hypotheses) are built and compared on GR misfit and geological plausibility; StarSteer supports multiple interpretations per lateral.
physical_constraints: Layer ordering from the typewell; locally planar beds (piecewise-constant apparent dip); faults as discrete vertical throws at segment boundaries; thickness scaling (stretch/squeeze, variable-thickness multi-typewell); TVT extremum where inclination equals apparent dip; consistency with 3D surfaces and neighbour wells.
dataset: Not applicable (practice). H&P Bayesian method validated on 1,440 synthetic laterals (layer cake + realistically corrupted gamma); H&P 2022 field test on two Haynesville wells (Sabine Oil & Gas).
synthetic_to_real: Humans work on real data only; alignment is by projecting the typewell parallel to modelled surfaces. H&P synthetic benchmark used geologically realistic layer cakes with corrupted gamma; no quantitative synthetic-to-real alignment stage reported.
metric_and_performance: No RMSE-type metric published. H&P 2022: automated interpretation matched human geosteerers on landing point, modelled structure and footage in zone for two wells; control-point interventions reduced to 0 and 2 after refinement. H&P 2023 Bayesian-Viterbi: comparable to their earlier automated method on 59% of 1,440 synthetic laterals, significantly better on 34%, 30x faster. Human context (see A02): in GWC 2021 only 14 of 329 participants scored >= 60%.
comparability: [uncertain] Low. No per-point TVT RMSE exists for manual or commercial methods. The Kaggle TVT labels are presumably produced by expert StarSteer-style interpretations, so manual practice defines the label-generating process rather than a comparable baseline.
validation_protocol: Not applicable for manual practice; H&P used synthetic trials and a two-well field test; no spatially grouped CV reported.
inference_budget: [uncertain] Manual: minutes per decision, hours per lateral. H&P 2023 Viterbi: 30x faster than their prior automated method (CPU, likely seconds per lateral).
repeated_layers: Handled by context rather than local match: continuity from the landing, multi-feature sequence and spacing matching, rejecting interpretations that need implausibly many dip changes or faults, and regional dip priors. Azimuthal gamma (up vs down) is the hardware remedy but is absent from the Kaggle data. Practitioners stress that one wrong pick propagates, i.e. errors are band-level and persistent.
drift: Handled explicitly through the dip state: a slow systematic TVT drift is exactly a small apparent-dip error, diagnosed via stretch/squeeze of GR features and fixed by re-dipping the segment, i.e. one parameter per segment rather than per point.
uncertainty_and_calibration: Traditional practice gives no uncertainty. Commercial automation offers heat maps / probabilities over stratigraphic depth and multi-scenario sets, but no published calibration (reliability/ECE) analysis.
where_to_use: (1) Output regulariser / post-hoc structure: a piecewise-linear-dip (few breakpoints) prior, either as a per-well refit of the expectation curve or as a training loss on the soft-argmax curve. (2) Input channels: typewell stretch/squeeze variants (already stubbed as tw_gr_m0p25 / tw_gr_p0p25 and gr_abs_diff_tw_m0p25 / gr_abs_diff_tw_p0p25 in experiments/arch/seq_NN_cfg.py, currently commented out). (3) Drift correction: per-well dip (slope) + offset re-estimation anchored on the known heel prefix. (4) Candidate generation: DP/Viterbi with a segment-count penalty as a propose-and-select candidate for a gate or averaging.
error_mode_targeted: Drift (~25%) primarily, via an explicit dip state; band confusion (~51%) secondarily, via continuity plus parsimony priors.
gap_vs_our_implementation: Already present: whole-lateral evidence (345 MD columns in one image), typewell-vs-lateral GR cost channel (gr_abs_diff), prefix conditioning (seen_tvt_rel, tw_seen_tvt_abs_diff), trajectory via z_diff, and the 2nd-place AnchorCNN+DP, which is a path-level method close to automated practice. Missing relative to expert practice: (a) no explicit dip/segment state or parsimony prior; the U-Net outputs an independent distribution per column and the expectation curve is not encouraged to be piecewise-linear, so a single-slope drift is not corrected as one parameter; (b) typewell stretch/squeeze (thickness variation) is not in the active channel set; (c) no scenario-level output with plausibility scores, band choice is implicit in per-column mass; (d) no explicit apparent-dip / inflection-point cue (inclination vs candidate dip); (e) experts use neighbours for regional dip and typewell selection rather than for picking humps, which may explain why our XY geo-prior hump picking failed. Note the post-hoc forward-backward continuity decode already failed, so continuity alone is insufficient; the specifically expert ingredient not yet tried is the low-complexity (few dip segments) constraint.
proposed_experiment: E0 (diagnostic, CPU): fit continuous piecewise-linear curves with a breakpoint penalty to the training-well TVT labels to measure how piecewise-linear the labels are (segments per 1000 ft, residual RMS); this sets K/lambda for E1/E3 and tests the label-provenance hypothesis. E1 (post-hoc, CPU): new script posterior_segment_refit.py next to posterior_fb_decode.py; on posterior dumps (results/baseline_check_posterior_all), fit TVT(MD) as continuous piecewise-linear with a per-breakpoint penalty to the expectation curve, weighted by inverse posterior variance and anchored to the prefix; output alpha*refit + (1-alpha)*mean with alpha in {0, 0.25, 0.5, 1}; control = raw expectation on the same 155 holdout wells; report pooled RMSE and the drift/band/hump decomposition from posterior_analysis.py. E2 (training, low effort): re-enable tw_gr_m0p25, tw_gr_p0p25, gr_abs_diff_tw_m0p25, gr_abs_diff_tw_p0p25 in unet_static_channels (experiments/arch/seq_NN_cfg.py); 60-epoch ConvNeXt vs baseline with 2 seeds each because of the +-0.39 ft noise floor. E3 (training, medium): add an L1 penalty on the second difference of the soft-argmax TVT curve along MD (total variation of dip, which favours piecewise-linear and tolerates rare jumps) with small weight; 60-epoch comparison. E4 (medium-high): DP over (TVT, dip) states with emissions from the U-Net column posterior and a breakpoint penalty, used only as a gate/average candidate, not as a replacement for the mean decode.
implementation_effort: E0/E1 low (numpy/scipy on existing dumps, about a day); E2 low (config toggle, feature code exists); E3 medium (loss term plus weight tuning); E4 medium-high (2D-state DP; must differ materially from the failed continuity decode).
gpu_cost: [uncertain] E0/E1: none (CPU, seconds per well). E2/E3: one 60-epoch ConvNeXt run per seed on the RTX 5060 8 GB, comparable to existing baseline runs (a few hours each). E4: inference-only.
distillation_compatibility: E2/E3 change teacher inputs/loss and transfer through KD on posteriors (the student needs the extra channels for E2). E1/E4 are post-hoc on any posterior and apply equally to the FastViT student.
error_correlation_with_ours: Segment refit or dip-state DP uses our posterior as emission, so band-choice errors remain highly correlated; diversity is limited to drift-shaped errors. Low value as an independent blend member, moderate as a structured corrector.
risk: The network may already produce near-piecewise-linear expectation curves, leaving little headroom. A hard refit can snap a hedged curve onto one band and raise RMSE, like other mode-seeking decodes. Stretch/squeeze channels were commented out upstream, possibly because they did not help. Faults (vertical throws) violate smoothness priors unless jumps are allowed. Gains may sit inside the +-0.39 ft noise floor. Azimuthal gamma, the strongest human cue for up/down ambiguity, is unavailable in the data.
notes: [uncertain] Label provenance: the ROGII competition TVT labels are likely StarSteer expert interpretations, which would make labels piecewise-linear dip segments with fault jumps; verify with E0 before investing in E1/E3. Commercial trend (StarSteer 2025.2 multi-typewell variable thickness, H&P 2023 Bayesian multi-solution) is toward probabilistic multi-scenario interpretation, i.e. a calibrated per-column posterior plus a scenario generator, which aligns with our direction. Related: H&P 2020 'Automated Geosteering with Fault Detection and Multi-Solution Tracking' (SPE/IADC DC 2020) and ROGII-GWC patent family US12421837 (adaptive combined heatmaps) not read in full.
